The *Kapparukkhiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 42) is a verse narrative preserved in the *Therāpadāna*, a late canonical collection of biographical poems in the Khuddaka Nikāya [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. Belonging to the *apadāna* genre, the text presents the past-life meritorious deeds and karmic attainments of the elder thera Kapparukkhiya [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. While modern scholarly discussion dedicated specifically to this poem remains scarce in the surveyed literature, SuttaCentral records five modern translations in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No external cross-language parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit corpora are attested in SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus records extensive Pali-internal text reuse, with 88 matching passages shared across 30 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Substantial segments are preserved and cited in commentary literature, notably the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §0.3–6.3 with high similarity) and the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In addition, formulaic verses and structural phrasing are widely shared with other Therāpadāna texts, such as the *Pallaṅkadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 152), *Tivaṇṭipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 192), *Tikicchakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 181), and the preceding *Dhammacakkikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 41) [DharmaNexus].
